news.headline: Vijayan demands action over SMA clinical trial drugs given to affected children
news.story_lead: Vijayan demands action over SMA clinical trial drugs given to affected children Thiruvananthapuram, Former Keralam Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan on Tuesday expressed shock over reports of experimental drugs meant for SMA clinical trials being given to children suffering from the genetic disease without their parents' consent and demanded strict action against those responsible. Vijayan, in a statement, said that the distribution of experimental medicines for spinal muscular atrophy afflicted children without the informed consent of their parents cannot be taken lightly and demanded an investigation into the matter. The Leader of the Opposition also accused State Health Minister K Muraleedharan of being indifferent to the issue and questioned whether children suffering from serious diseases were being turned into test subjects.
news.full_article_text: Vijayan demands action over SMA clinical trial drugs given to affected children Thiruvananthapuram, Former Keralam Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan on Tuesday expressed shock over reports of experimental drugs meant for SMA clinical trials being given to children suffering from the genetic disease without their parents' consent and demanded strict action against those responsible. Vijayan, in a statement, said that the distribution of experimental medicines for spinal muscular atrophy afflicted children without the informed consent of their parents cannot be taken lightly and demanded an investigation into the matter. The Leader of the Opposition also accused State Health Minister K Muraleedharan of being indifferent to the issue and questioned whether children suffering from serious diseases were being turned into test subjects. His remarks come in the wake of news reports of parents claiming that SMA drugs distributed through the Sree Avittom Thirunal Hospital here were marked as 'Physician Sample' and 'For Clinical Trials Only'. "This is a blatant violation of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act and the storage rules. The Health Department cannot avoid responsibility for this," the CPI veteran said. Earlier in the day, Muraleedharan told reporters that it was done according to a circular issued by the previous government. He said that more details about it can be gathered from Dr Mini at SAT Hospital, who is the expert on the issue. "The minister may not know about every medicine," he told reporters. Referring to the minister's response, Vijayan termed it as "shocking and cruel" and accused the former of handling the issue "very irresponsibly". "This is the latest sign that Keralam's health sector has collapsed in every way in the last five months," he said. The Leader of the Opposition also accused the government of gambling with the lives of kids. Vijayan claimed that the administration took such a decision by ignoring the strong opposition against it as well as concerns of the patients' association 'Cure SMA'. He further claimed that he brought the issue to the government's attention via a letter, but has not received any response to it and no action has been taken on it. news.headline: Rubio hails ‘great’ meeting with Jaishankar, UAE foreign minister on regional energy security
news.story_lead: Rubio hails ‘great’ meeting with Jaishankar, UAE foreign minister on regional energy security US secretary of state Marco Rubio is arrived in Mumbai on Tuesday for a three-day visit to India. US secretary of state Marco Rubio, who is in India on a three-day visit, held a trilateral meeting with India's minister of external affairs S Jaishankar and UAE's foreign minister Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan on Tuesday. Rubio later said he held a ‘great’ meeting with the two leaders where they discussed regional energy security and way ahead on shared economic priorities.
news.full_article_text: Rubio hails ‘great’ meeting with Jaishankar, UAE foreign minister on regional energy security US secretary of state Marco Rubio is arrived in Mumbai on Tuesday for a three-day visit to India. US secretary of state Marco Rubio, who is in India on a three-day visit, held a trilateral meeting with India's minister of external affairs S Jaishankar and UAE's foreign minister Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan on Tuesday. Rubio later said he held a ‘great’ meeting with the two leaders where they discussed regional energy security and way ahead on shared economic priorities. Track live updates on Day 1 of Rubio's India visit The UAE leader arrived in India for a two-day visit on Monday evening, following which he attended the meeting with Rubio and Jaishankar on Tuesday. Rubio also expressed support for India's efforts to diversify its energy portfolio despite its continued purchases of Russian crude oil. He said, “I think what India has expressed repeatedly is its desire to diversify its energy portfolio, which is a smart thing to do. It's not easy to do that from one day to the next. I think they've made some substantial progress in that regard, and we're happy to see that.” Also read: ‘India diversified imports, but hard to pivot in one day’: Marco Rubio explains why US waived some Russia energy tariffs On India's purchase of Russian oil, Rubio said, "But in the end, it's not just about Russian oil; it's about India's desire to diversify, and we think we can be a source of some of its energy inputs. We've discussed Venezuela and other countries, and I think it's in our interest to have strong allies with diverse energy portfolios." Rubio's India visit Rubio arrived in Mumbai on Tuesday for his second visit to India this year. India and the US are expected to explore ways to strengthen cooperation in key areas, including defence, security, technology and critical minerals. Also read: 'Very, very close, some items left': Marco Rubio on India-US trade deal The US leader also backed the idea of talks between the United States, Russia and China on arms control, saying dialogue among the three major nuclear powers would be beneficial for global peace. Speaking in Mumbai, Rubio said US President Donald Trump had expressed openness to discussions at the leaders’ level. He said communication was essential to diplomacy, even between countries with strong disagreements, but added that he was unsure whether China was willing to participate. Rubio said Beijing had historically maintained that it would discuss arms control only after catching up with other nuclear powers. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR HT News Desk Follow the latest breaking news, major developments and agenda-setting stories from India and around the world with the newsdesk at Hindustan Times. news.exam_corner_topic: Supreme Court transfers trial of corruption case against retd HC judge to Delhi
news.headline: Supreme Court transfers trial of corruption case against retd HC judge to Delhi
news.story_lead: Supreme Court transfers trial of corruption case against retd HC judge to Delhi The order was passed on October 14 by a bench of CJI Surya Kant and justice Joymalya Bagchi in a transfer petition filed by the former judge. The Supreme Court has directed the trial of a disproportionate assets case against former Allahabad high court judge, justice (retd) Shri Narayan Shukla, to be transferred from Lucknow to a Delhi court hearing a corruption case against him. The order was passed on October 14 by a bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and justice Joymalya Bagchi in a transfer petition filed by the former judge.
news.full_article_text: Supreme Court transfers trial of corruption case against retd HC judge to Delhi The order was passed on October 14 by a bench of CJI Surya Kant and justice Joymalya Bagchi in a transfer petition filed by the former judge. The Supreme Court has directed the trial of a disproportionate assets case against former Allahabad high court judge, justice (retd) Shri Narayan Shukla, to be transferred from Lucknow to a Delhi court hearing a corruption case against him. The order was passed on October 14 by a bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and justice Joymalya Bagchi in a transfer petition filed by the former judge. Shukla retired in July 2020 after he was accused of taking a bribe to pass an order favouring Prasad Institute of Medical Sciences – a Lucknow-based medical college debarred in May 2017 from admitting students by the Medical Council of India (MCI). A charge sheet was filed against Shukla by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) in the corruption case, and the trial is pending before a Delhi court. During this investigation, CBI lodged another criminal case in 2023 against the former judge for allegedly acquiring disproportionate assets worth over ₹ 2.5 crore between 2014 and 2019. This case, too, was registered by CBI but the trial proceeded before a Lucknow CBI court. Since the present proceedings emerged from the earlier corruption case, Shukla sought the transfer of the Lucknow trial to Delhi. Allowing the petition, the top court order said, “Sessions Case No.737/2026 titled “CBI v. Narayan Shukla & Anr.”, which is pending before the Court of Special Judge, Anti-Corruption, CBI, West Lucknow, U.P. is ordered to be transferred to the Court of Special Judge (PC Act) CBI, Rouse Avenue Court, Central District, New Delhi.” The court also directed the accused along with his family members named in the DA case to fully cooperate with the trial without seeking any unnecessary adjournment. The court further told CBI to identify such official witnesses who can be examined through video conferencing to ensure the trial is expedited. Advocate Sanjay Mani Tripathi, who appeared for the former judge, argued before the top court that the DA proceedings arise out of the same FIR and charge sheet in the alleged bribery case pending in Delhi. He said that although the FIR in the DA case was filed in Delhi, the trial was held in Lucknow. CBI, represented by additional solicitor general (ASG) Davinder Pal Singh, did not oppose the request, saying it has no objection if the court of competent jurisdiction in Delhi conducts both trials. CBI has already filed a charge sheet in the DA case as well. The alleged bribery case took place when, as a judge of the Allahabad high court, Shukla passed an order on August 25, 2017 in favour of Prakash Education Trust, allowing the debarred college to admit students. CBI registered a case against the former judge and others in December 2019, which resulted in a charge sheet filed in December 2021 before the Special Judge hearing CBI cases in the Rouse Avenue Courts. The investigators allege that Shukla facilitated the order in conspiracy with retired Orissa high court judge, justice (retd) IM Quddusi, along with the Prasad Medical College owners Bhagwan Prasad Yadav and Palash Yadav, and Bhawana Pandey acting as an intermediary along with Sudhir Giri. Prasad Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) was barred by the Medical Council of India over substandard facilities. It was one of 47 medical colleges restrained from admitting students for the admission years 2017-18 and 2018-19. According to CBI, PIMS challenged the MCI decision before the top court. However, it later withdrew the petition and filed a fresh plea in the high court. Shukla allegedly met the owner of PIMS along with former judge Qudussi at his residence pursuant to which the favourable order was passed by a bench comprising Shukla. CBI approached the then-CJI Dipak Misra to conduct a probe against Shukla, then a sitting judge of the high court. An in-house committee constituted by the then CJI concluded that Shukla was guilty of judicial malpractice which established the ground for his removal under the Constitution. Based on the report, all judicial and administrative work was withdrawn from Shukla even as the probe against him continued. In July 2019, CBI approached the then-CJI Ranjan Gogoi for permission to prosecute the former judge. Gogoi granted the permission and even recommended to the Centre that Shukla be removed. Even as the matter remained pending, Shukla retired in July 2020. - Allahabad High Court

news.story_lead: RSS, Bengal finance minister condemn vandalism at Left book stalls during Durga Puja CPI(M), CPI and CPI(ML) Liberation have alleged attacks on or removal of their book stalls near Durga Puja pandals across Kolkata and other districts. The Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) and a senior Bengal cabinet minister have condemned the back-to-back vandalism at Left book stalls by alleged Right-wing groups in West Bengal on Monday. “The RSS never supports such vandalism and destruction of books.
news.full_article_text: RSS, Bengal finance minister condemn vandalism at Left book stalls during Durga Puja CPI(M), CPI and CPI(ML) Liberation have alleged attacks on or removal of their book stalls near Durga Puja pandals across Kolkata and other districts. The Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) and a senior Bengal cabinet minister have condemned the back-to-back vandalism at Left book stalls by alleged Right-wing groups in West Bengal on Monday. “The RSS never supports such vandalism and destruction of books. We condemn such acts of cowardice. All people have the right to express views,” said Jishnu Basu, prachar pramukh of the RSS's east zonal unit. Also Read: After stampede deaths, Bengal Oppn targets BJP, unites over Left book stalls “We have not been able to identify these people. We don't know who sent them,” Basu told HT, referring to viral videos uploaded from various parts of Kolkata and the districts. The stalls have been set up by the CPI(M) , CPI and CPI(ML) Liberation. Since last week, all three parties have alleged that book stalls set up near community Durga Puja pandals in Kolkata and the districts were either ransacked by members of various Hindutva groups or removed by the police, who cited a lack of permission. Bengal finance minister Swapan Dasgupta also condemned the vandalism. Also Read: Vehicles near Amit Shah’s rally in Bengal vandalised, BJP blames TMC “These incidents have made me hang my head in shame. I have been a staunch critic of the Left all my life and continue to be so. But that does not mean someone can stop the Left parties from displaying or selling their books. Who are these vandals?” Dasgupta told the media. CPI(M) central committee member Sujan Chakraborty, however, dismissed the claims. “Jishnu Basu and Swapan Dasgupta are trying to be naive. These acts of vandalism started under the patronage of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). Chief minister Suvendu Adhikari said in the assembly that he would not allow these book stalls unless we met his conditions,” Chakraborty said. Adhikari had said in the legislative assembly on September 10 that he would ask community Durga Puja committees to allow CPI(M) and other Left book stalls near their pandals only if the parties referred to the festival as Durga Puja instead of Sharodotsav (autumn festival), a term Bengal's communists have traditionally used because of their atheist beliefs. Several videos that surfaced after the vandalism purportedly showed the perpetrators claiming to be acting on Adhikari's orders. “How dare they carry out vandalism in our name!” Dasgupta said. news.exam_corner_topic: Marco Rubio to arrive in India today; trade, security and technology on agenda
news.headline: Marco Rubio to arrive in India today; trade, security and technology on agenda
news.story_lead: Marco Rubio to arrive in India today; trade, security and technology on agenda Discussions are expected to cover energy, technology, security and critical minerals, alongside the effects of conflicts in Ukraine and West Asia. India and the US are expected to focus on ways to take forward cooperation in key areas ranging from defence and security to technology and critical minerals when external affairs minister S Jaishankar meets secretary of state Marco Rubio in Mumbai on Tuesday against the backdrop of continuing strains in bilateral relations. Rubio is set to arrive in the financial hub with a large business delegation on Tuesday afternoon after a visit to Uzbekistan.
news.full_article_text: Marco Rubio to arrive in India today; trade, security and technology on agenda Discussions are expected to cover energy, technology, security and critical minerals, alongside the effects of conflicts in Ukraine and West Asia. India and the US are expected to focus on ways to take forward cooperation in key areas ranging from defence and security to technology and critical minerals when external affairs minister S Jaishankar meets secretary of state Marco Rubio in Mumbai on Tuesday against the backdrop of continuing strains in bilateral relations. Rubio is set to arrive in the financial hub with a large business delegation on Tuesday afternoon after a visit to Uzbekistan. This is his second visit to India since May, when he held bilateral talks with Jaishankar and joined a Quad foreign ministers’ meeting in New Delhi . Rubio is also travelling to India days after President Donald Trump waived provisions of the Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act (SRIA) that authorised punitive tariffs on countries buying Russian oil. While India has already made its concerns about SRIA – including the potential impact on bilateral ties and the global energy market – known to the US administration, the talks between Jaishankar and Rubio are expected to focus on maintaining the momentum in India-US relations and stepping up cooperation in trade, energy, technology and critical minerals, people familiar with the matter said on condition of anonymity. Also Read | US ‘very close’ to India trade deal; energy needs considered in Russia sanctions waiver: Marco Rubio The two leaders are also expected to discuss regional and global issues, including the conflicts in Ukraine and West Asia, and their fallout on food, fuel and fertiliser security, the people said. The Indian side has made a proposal for a Russia-Ukraine ceasefire that is aimed at ensuring the flow of energy and food supplies and preventing attacks on merchant shipping in the Black Sea. Potential meetings between the leadership of the two sides on the margins of multilateral events such as the Asean Summit in Manila next month and the G20 Summit in Florida in the US are also expected to figure in the discussions. Jaishankar will also attend a celebration marking the 250th anniversary of the independence of the US as the guest of honour. Relations between India and the US have been impacted by strains over the past year, largely because of the Trump administration’s trade and tariff policies, as well as its restrictions that impact Indian professionals and its burgeoning relationship with Pakistan. Negotiations for a bilateral trade agreement appear to be stalled, with officials talking about both sides trying to find a landing point for a deal. Also Read | Government defends Jaishankar-Rubio Mumbai meeting amid opposition backlash Rubio’s itinerary includes Reliance Industries’ refinery at Jamnagar in Gujarat, a key processor of Russian oil that he is expected to visit for a few hours on October 21. Reliance is investing in a massive refinery to be set up in Texas, the first new project of its kind in the US in five decades, and is also a significant purchaser of Venezuelan oil, the sales of which are controlled by the Trump administration. Ahead of his arrival in India, Rubio acknowledged India’s reliance on Russian energy despite a diversification of sources by noting that “it’s hard to pivot” on oil suppliers, and said that Trump intends to use 60-day period for waivers under the SRIA to analyse what sanctions and tariffs mean to the global economy. Before Rubio’s visit, US ambassador Sergio Gor’s remarks that the US side expected Jaishankar to be in Mumbai to meet Rubio invited criticism from the Opposition. The external affairs ministry, however, said it has been the practice over the past decade for India to host foreign dignitaries outside Delhi. Also Read | Russia sanctions pause to assess impact on India, global energy prices, says Trump official Ahead of Rubio’s arrival, Jaishankar will meet the deputy prime minister and foreign minister of the United Arab Emirates (UAE), Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan, over dinner on Monday night. They are expected to review bilateral cooperation and take forward initiatives in energy, trade, investments, defence, as well as discuss the situation in West Asia. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Rezaul H Laskar Rezaul Hasan Laskar is Foreign Editor with the Hindustan Times, which he joined in 2015. He began as a journalist in his hometown of Shillong in northeast India and has worked in newspapers and wire services over the years. He moved to New Delhi in 1997 and initially focused on defence, national security, Jammu and Kashmir and the northeast, while also working of foreign policy and international relations. He has been part of the media delegation accompanying PMs on foreign visits and has reported from destinations ranging from Tibet to Ukraine. Between 2007 and 2013, he was the Press Trust of India correspondent in Pakistan, one of only two Indian journalists allowed to report from the country. He extensively covered Pakistan’s domestic politics and the life of the common people, as well as the fallout of the 2008 Mumbai attacks on India-Pakistan relations and the subsequent trial in Pakistan of the suspects involved in the attack. As part of his reportage in Pakistan, he travelled the breadth of the country, from the Swat Valley to Balochistan. Reza’s first gig in journalism was writing a weekly music column, and music – especially classic rock – remains a keen interest. He is also a movie buff and a keen photographer. Read More

news.exam_corner_topic: Supreme Court seeks law reform proposals to protect people from Northeast by Dec 18
news.headline: Supreme Court seeks law reform proposals to protect people from Northeast by Dec 18
news.story_lead: Supreme Court seeks law reform proposals to protect people from Northeast by Dec 18 The bench directed authorities to record complainants’ addresses and other details immediately after receiving harassment complaints. The Supreme Court has directed the committee constituted by the Centre to monitor complaints of violence and harassment against people from the Northeast region living in other parts of the country and recommend necessary changes in law for their protection by December 18. In an order passed on October 14, the top court further directed the committee to ensure that in future, victims’ statements are recorded soon after the incident to avoid delay in tracing them.
news.full_article_text: Supreme Court seeks law reform proposals to protect people from Northeast by Dec 18 The bench directed authorities to record complainants’ addresses and other details immediately after receiving harassment complaints. The Supreme Court has directed the committee constituted by the Centre to monitor complaints of violence and harassment against people from the Northeast region living in other parts of the country and recommend necessary changes in law for their protection by December 18. In an order passed on October 14, the top court further directed the committee to ensure that in future, victims’ statements are recorded soon after the incident to avoid delay in tracing them. Manipur music teacher’s killing brings focus back to safety concerns The order comes close on the heels of the recent killing of a 54-year-old music teacher from Manipur , Vikram Singh Chongtham, in Delhi last month by a group of men after he asked them not to create a commotion outside his house. The bench of justices Sanjay Kumar and Sanjeev Sachdeva said, “The committee shall also address the issue of necessary changes being made in the law to ensure protection and make suitable recommendations to the authorities concerned after due consideration.” The order passed in a petition filed by advocate Alana Golmei gives an impetus to the long-standing demand of criminal law reforms to strengthen the institutional mechanism available to tackle incidents of violence against people from northeast living in other parts of the country. Also read: ‘Clothes torn, hit with bamboo stick’: 2 women from Assam and Bihar molested, racially abused outside Delhi club Bezbaruah committee had proposed specific legal amendments In 2014, following the death of Nido Tania, a student from Arunachal Pradesh , in Delhi, the Centre set up a committee headed by former IAS officer MK Bezbaruah, that recommended changes in the Indian Penal Code (IPC) among other set of reforms concerning issues faced by northeastern people. Two specific changes were recommended by the Bezbaruah committee seeking introduction of new provisions section 153C dealing with hate speech and section 505A on provocation of violence on grounds of race, caste, place of birth, residence, etc. In 2017, the Law Commission of India made similar recommendations to the Centre for inserting the two provisions. The Monitoring Committee was constituted by the Centre in 2016 on a PIL proceeding filed by Karma Dorjee. One of the mandates assigned to the committee was to ensure implementation of the Bezbaruah committee recommendations. However, though the issue of law reforms to prevent racial discrimination of Northeast people was discussed, no concrete recommendations have been made by the committee so far. Also read: Couple held for racial abuse of northeast women; charges under SC/ST Act slapped Nine complaints of violence and harassment reviewed by panel Posting the matter on December 18, the court went through an affidavit filed by the Centre giving details of the proceedings of the Monitoring Committee that met on September 8. The committee dealt with nine cases of violence and harassment reported across the country against northeasterns over the past one year and the action taken by the police in the respective states. The bench was informed that in some cases, the complaints could not be acted upon as the complainant was untraceable. To avoid delay in pursuing the complaints in future, the court held, “Henceforth, measures shall be put in place to immediately record the full details, including addresses, of the complainants as and when complaints of any harassment are received and necessary further action shall be initiated without fail.” The court also pulled up the committee for showing lack of “seriousness” in attending the meetings. Going by the minutes of the meeting held last month, only three out of the 11-member committee attended the meeting physically while the remaining connected virtually through video-conferencing. Not satisfied by such an approach, the bench said, “It is distressing to note that out of the committee members, only three attended the meeting physically and even those, who were stationed in Delhi, including two under secretaries to the Government of India , participated in the meeting through video-conferencing.” In February this year, the court had directed the committee to meet at least once in three months. “It would be advisable to fix the actual date of the next meeting as per the convenience of the committee members,” the order said. Also read: AMU teacher alleges online harassment over Northeast identity; FIR registered SC says targeting people over cultural or racial differences is unacceptable The top court while hearing the present case early this year had observed that targeting people because of cultural or racial differences is unacceptable. The instances of hate crimes and racial discrimination against northeasterns still continues. In December last year, Anjel Chakma, a MBA student was attacked along with his brother while they were shopping in Selaqui area of Dehradun in Uttarakhand. The Angel Chakma case is one of the nine incidents being overseen by the monitoring committee set up by the MHA . The other cases pertain to Delhi, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, and Maharashtra.

news.full_article_text: No irregularity in Parliament not being prorogued: Kiren Rijiju The minister cited past instances when the Lok Sabha remained unprorogued for up to 87 days, arguing that the gap after adjournment did not constitute violation Union minister Kiren Rijiju said on Monday said there was no impropriety or irregularity in Parliament not being prorogued since the monsoon session ended in August as there was “no constitutional requirement” prescribing a specific period within which a House must be prorogued following its adjournment sine die. news.headline: Army’s communications satellite likely by mid-2028: Top officials
news.story_lead: Army’s communications satellite likely by mid-2028: Top officials The Indian Army’s first dedicated communications satellite is expected to be launched by the Indian Space Research Organisation (Isro) around mid-2028, reinforcing the force’s communications backbone and its operational capabilities, top officials aware of the matter said on Monday. The satellite, GSAT-7B, will provide the army with secure, round-the-clock connectivity across remote border areas and challenging terrain, supporting day-to-day military operations and effective battlefield command and control, the officials said. The development is significant because the army, unlike the Indian Air Force and the navy, lacks a dedicated communications satellite and currently relies on the IAF’s GSAT-7A to meet its communication requirements.
news.full_article_text: Army’s communications satellite likely by mid-2028: Top officials The Indian Army’s first dedicated communications satellite is expected to be launched by the Indian Space Research Organisation (Isro) around mid-2028, reinforcing the force’s communications backbone and its operational capabilities, top officials aware of the matter said on Monday. The satellite, GSAT-7B, will provide the army with secure, round-the-clock connectivity across remote border areas and challenging terrain, supporting day-to-day military operations and effective battlefield command and control, the officials said. The development is significant because the army, unlike the Indian Air Force and the navy, lacks a dedicated communications satellite and currently relies on the IAF’s GSAT-7A to meet its communication requirements. In March 2023, the defence ministry signed a ₹ 3,000-crore contract with NewSpace India Limited (NSIL), Isro’s commercial arm, to develop the advanced communications satellite for the army—a step towards addressing a long-standing requirement. The launch, initially scheduled for November 2027, will be delayed by six months due to technical reasons, the officials added, asking not to be named. The five-tonne geostationary satellite, India’s heaviest communications satellite so far, is designed to provide beyond-line-of-sight communications for deployed troops and military formations, as well as weapon systems, airborne platforms and other mission-critical assets. Space-based communications will be critical during conflict, providing resilient communication links when terrestrial networks are disrupted or damaged by enemy action, the officials said. Last week, the defence ministry signed a ₹ 2,563-crore contract with NSIL for another dedicated communications satellite, GSAT-7C, for the IAF. The indigenously designed, developed and manufactured satellite will enhance secure, resilient and seamless communication capabilities for the IAF’s assets, strengthening operational effectiveness, it said. Isro launched the navy’s GSAT-7R communications satellite last November, a replacement for the Rukmini satellite. The home-grown satellite enables seamless and secure communications between warships, aircraft, submarines and maritime operations centres. The Indian military’s focus on space has been steadily growing. It released the Joint Military Space Doctrine last September during the Combined Commanders’ Conference in Kolkata, a significant step towards institutionalising space as a key domain of national security and integrating it into the country’s defence strategy. The country is also formulating a National Military Space Policy to safeguard its space-based assets, strengthen military capabilities and address emerging security challenges in the space domain. India plans to launch 52 dedicated military satellites over the next three years under Phase III of its Space Based Surveillance (SBS) mission, approved by the Prime Minister-led Cabinet Committee on Security in October 2024. Spearheaded by the Defence Space Agency under the HQ Integrated Defence Staff, the ₹ 26,968-crore project involves Isro constructing and launching 21 satellites, with private companies handling the remaining 31. To be sure, China is expanding its space capabilities rapidly and can potentially disable or knock out satellites. It is known to possess capabilities to disrupt satellite signals using jammers as well as other anti-satellite technologies.

hindi_translation.full_article_text:

फिलिस्तीनी कार्यकर्ता महमूद खलील ने ट्रम्प प्रशासन से जुड़ी नीतियों के तहत किए जा रहे देशनिकाला प्रयासों को रोकने के लिए संयुक्त राज्य अमेरिका के सुप्रीम कोर्ट का दरवाजा खटखटाया है।

यह याचिका डोनाल्ड ट्रम्प प्रशासन की नीतियों के तहत शुरू किए गए देशनिकाला प्रयासों को चुनौती देती है।

hindi_translation.story_lead: एशियाई पैरा खेल 2026 में भारतीय पैरा-तीरंदाज शीतल देवी और स्वाति चौधरी ने अपनी-अपनी श्रेणियों के फाइनल में प्रवेश कर लिया है। इसके साथ ही दीप्ति जीवनजी ने 400 मीटर टी20 स्पर्धा में रिकॉर्ड के साथ स्वर्ण पदक जीता और मनीष नरवाल ने शूटिंग में रजत पदक जीतकर एलए 2028 कोटा हासिल किया।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### एशियाई पैरा खेल 2026 में प्रमुख उपलब्धियां

भारतीय पैरा-तीरंदाज शीतल देवी और स्वाति चौधरी ने एशियाई पैरा खेल 2026 में बेहतरीन प्रदर्शन करते हुए फाइनल में जगह बनाई। विश्व रिकॉर्ड धारक शीतल देवी ने प्रतियोगिता के दौरान अपना शानदार प्रदर्शन जारी रखा। मिश्रित टीमों ने भी आगे कदम बढ़ाए, हालांकि भारत को कुछ व्यक्तिगत दौरों में असफलताओं का सामना भी करना पड़ा।

### अन्य प्रमुख पदक विजेता

- **दीप्ति जीवनजी (एथलेटिक्स):** महिलाओं की 400 मीटर T20 स्पर्धा में एशियाई पैरा खेल रिकॉर्ड के साथ स्वर्ण पदक जीता।
- **मनीष नरवाल (शूटिंग):** 10 मीटर एयर पिस्टल SH1 स्पर्धा में रजत पदक जीता और लॉस एंजिल्स 2028 पैरालिंपिक खेलों के लिए कोटा हासिल किया।
- **अशोक (पावरलिफ्टिंग):** पुरुषों के 65 किग्रा पावरलिफ्टिंग में रजत पदक जीता।
- **प्रदीप कुमार (एथलेटिक्स):** भाला फेंक स्पर्धा में रजत पदक हासिल किया।
- **रिंकू हुड्डा (एथलेटिक्स):** भारत के लिए स्वर्ण पदक जीता।
- **भाविना पटेल (टेबल टेनिस):** कांस्य पदक अपने नाम किया।

news.headline: Child rights panel files case over Keralam boy’s malnutrition death
news.story_lead: Child rights panel files case over Keralam boy’s malnutrition death A 2-year-old in Kerala died amid suspected malnutrition. Authorities are investigating possible neglect and have taken the couple’s four children into care. A two-year-old boy died in a suspected case of malnutrition in the Alappuzha district of Keralam, officials said on Monday, with the Kerala State Commission for Protection of Child Rights registering a case.
news.full_article_text: Child rights panel files case over Keralam boy’s malnutrition death A 2-year-old in Kerala died amid suspected malnutrition. Authorities are investigating possible neglect and have taken the couple’s four children into care. A two-year-old boy died in a suspected case of malnutrition in the Alappuzha district of Keralam, officials said on Monday, with the Kerala State Commission for Protection of Child Rights registering a case. The Child Welfare Committee has meanwhile taken the couple’s four children under its care amid allegations of parental neglect. The deceased, Rahul, was the sixth child of Rajesh, an autorickshaw driver, and Thara, a homemaker who resided in a crumbling rental house in Karthikappally. The two-year-old, found unresponsive by his father early Sunday at their home, was declared dead at a government hospital in Haripad. Another child of the couple had also died a few years ago, officials said, though no clear reasons were attributed to that death. A senior inspector in Thrikkunnapuzha police station, where a case for unnatural death was registered, said a postmortem examination was conducted in Alappuzha following suspicions of negligence. “The autopsy report stated that the child was severely anaemic. He also weighed only 7.6 kg, significantly less than the average 12 kg expected for a child of his age. These findings indicate that he was not getting adequate nutritious food,” the officer said, adding that a histopathology test was conducted to identify the exact cause of death and the report is awaited. CWC officials have taken the couple’s four children into their care while the mother, who delivered her seventh child last week, remains in a hospital with the newborn, officials said. A statement by the KSCPCR said that it has sought explanations from the district medical officer, the secretary of Karthikappally grama panchayat, the district child protection officer and the integrated child development services supervisor of the panchayat. Minister for women and child development Bindhu Krishna termed the death “extremely painful.” “It is particularly painful because the W&C department has intervened multiple times to ensure better care of the children. We even shifted them to a shelter home....,” she said. Babitha Jayan, a district panchayat member in Alappuzha, said: “When the mother was recently pregnant with her seventh child, we shifted her and the kids to Gandhi Bhavan. They were being provided food and medical help. But within two weeks, they returned to their rental home.” “When we tried to intervene, the mother threatened that she would die by suicide along with the kids. We were forced to take a few steps back,” she said. The official also said that the parents refused to send their children to school and neglected them. Home minister Ramesh Chennithala said that the family is from his constituency and the matter has come to his notice. “If any assistance needs to be provided from the government’s side, we are ready to provide it. I have sent people there, including the concerned Tahsildar. After examining it, they have been asked to provide a report,” he told reporters. A local ASHA worker said, “The mother would buy a packet of milk, add water to it and give a glass to the elder children, asking them to feed the two-year-old. Somehow, it was the responsibility of the elder children to feed their younger brother.” Malnutrition and starvation deaths, particularly among children, are rare in Keralam owing to the state’s superior public health infrastructure and social standards. Keralam’s neo natal mortality rate of 5, as per the 2022 Sample Registration System report, is the lowest in the country. India’s average is 19. Early child mortality rate (deaths below 5 years of age) in Keralam, as per the SRS report, was 9, the lowest in the country. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Vishnu Varma Vishnu Varma is Assistant Editor and reports from Kerala for the Hindustan Times. He has 10 years of experience writing for print and digital platforms and has worked at The New York Times, NDTV and The Indian Express in the past. He specialises in longform reportage at the intersections of politics, crime, social commentary and environment. Read More

hindi_translation.full_article_text: Child rights panel files case over Keralam boy’s malnutrition death A 2-year-old in Kerala died amid suspected malnutrition. Authorities are investigating possible neglect and have taken the couple’s four children into care. A two-year-old boy died in a suspected case of malnutrition in the Alappuzha district of Keralam, officials said on Monday, with the Kerala State Commission for Protection of Child Rights registering a case. The Child Welfare Committee has meanwhile taken the couple’s four children under its care amid allegations of parental neglect. The deceased, Rahul, was the sixth child of Rajesh, an autorickshaw driver, and Thara, a homemaker who resided in a crumbling rental house in Karthikappally. The two-year-old, found unresponsive by his father early Sunday at their home, was declared dead at a government hospital in Haripad. Another child of the couple had also died a few years ago, officials said, though no clear reasons were attributed to that death. A senior inspector in Thrikkunnapuzha police station, where a case for unnatural death was registered, said a postmortem examination was conducted in Alappuzha following suspicions of negligence. “The autopsy report stated that the child was severely anaemic. He also weighed only 7.6 kg, significantly less than the average 12 kg expected for a child of his age. These findings indicate that he was not getting adequate nutritious food,” the officer said, adding that a histopathology test was conducted to identify the exact cause of death and the report is awaited. CWC officials have taken the couple’s four children into their care while the mother, who delivered her seventh child last week, remains in a hospital with the newborn, officials said. A statement by the KSCPCR said that it has sought explanations from the district medical officer, the secretary of Karthikappally grama panchayat, the district child protection officer and the integrated child development services supervisor of the panchayat. Minister for women and child development Bindhu Krishna termed the death “extremely painful.” “It is particularly painful because the W&C department has intervened multiple times to ensure better care of the children. We even shifted them to a shelter home....,” she said. Babitha Jayan, a district panchayat member in Alappuzha, said: “When the mother was recently pregnant with her seventh child, we shifted her and the kids to Gandhi Bhavan. They were being provided food and medical help. But within two weeks, they returned to their rental home.” “When we tried to intervene, the mother threatened that she would die by suicide along with the kids. We were forced to take a few steps back,” she said. The official also said that the parents refused to send their children to school and neglected them. Home minister Ramesh Chennithala said that the family is from his constituency and the matter has come to his notice. “If any assistance needs to be provided from the government’s side, we are ready to provide it. I have sent people there, including the concerned Tahsildar. After examining it, they have been asked to provide a report,” he told reporters. A local ASHA worker said, “The mother would buy a packet of milk, add water to it and give a glass to the elder children, asking them to feed the two-year-old. Somehow, it was the responsibility of the elder children to feed their younger brother.” Malnutrition and starvation deaths, particularly among children, are rare in Keralam owing to the state’s superior public health infrastructure and social standards. Keralam’s neo natal mortality rate of 5, as per the 2022 Sample Registration System report, is the lowest in the country. India’s average is 19. Early child mortality rate (deaths below 5 years of age) in Keralam, as per the SRS report, was 9, the lowest in the country. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Vishnu Varma Vishnu Varma is Assistant Editor and reports from Kerala for the Hindustan Times. He has 10 years of experience writing for print and digital platforms and has worked at The New York Times, NDTV and The Indian Express in the past. He specialises in longform reportage at the intersections of politics, crime, social commentary and environment. Read More

news.exam_corner_topic: ‘We thought worst was behind us’: Shroff attack sends shockwaves through Bollywood
news.headline: ‘We thought worst was behind us’: Shroff attack sends shockwaves through Bollywood
news.story_lead: ‘We thought worst was behind us’: Shroff attack sends shockwaves through Bollywood The underworld’s stranglehold on Bollywood through the 1990s is still a raw memory Mumbai film industry The attack on actor Tiger Shroff on Sunday has had a chilling impact on the film industry in Mumbai. For many, the underworld’s stranglehold on Bollywood through the 1990s is still a raw memory. The attack on Shroff, whose father, Jackie, is a loved figure in the film industry, comes on the back of threats to several other stars.
news.full_article_text: ‘We thought worst was behind us’: Shroff attack sends shockwaves through Bollywood The underworld’s stranglehold on Bollywood through the 1990s is still a raw memory Mumbai film industry The attack on actor Tiger Shroff on Sunday has had a chilling impact on the film industry in Mumbai. For many, the underworld’s stranglehold on Bollywood through the 1990s is still a raw memory. The attack on Shroff, whose father, Jackie, is a loved figure in the film industry, comes on the back of threats to several other stars. Those who have been threatened in the last two years include Salman Khan, his brother-in-law, actor Ayush Sharma, director Rohit Shetty, and Ranveer Singh. Politician Baba Siddiqui, killed in October 2024, was a close friend of Bollywood A-listers including Salman Khan and Shah Rukh Khan. In the same month as Siddique’s killing, stand-up comic Munawar Faruqui was provided police cover after threats from the Bishnoi gang. In July this year, actor Aamir Khan was warned about indulging in ‘Love Jihad’ by the same gang following his wedding to Gauri Spratt. Deep Dive But what has rattled the Mumbai film industry is the audacity of the attack on Shroff from such close range. Three motorbike-borne men fired seven rounds from a sophisticated semi-automatic Zigana handgun at his car in Juhu at 7pm amid Navratri season when the area was choc-a-bloc with traffic. The attackers were unmasked and unconcerned about being caught. “They were also watching him. How else did they know that he routinely went to the Pushpa Narsee Park to play football every Sunday?” said a leading man who often plays football with Tiger Shroff at the same venue. In Mumbai, top stars have resorted to private security. “The attack on Tiger has taken us back to the 90s. I am just going to add a few more people to my retinue of bodyguards,” said a famous action star of the 1990s. “This attack has left me really frightened. I have three guards. But are they enough?” He added that if he, too, like his friends Salman Khan and Shetty, has to disappear behind a wall of security. Salman Khan has a Y Plus security in addition to a private detail. In June 2022, a note was left on the promenade at Bandra Bandstand for the actor’s screenwriter father, Salim Khan, at his usual bench, warning that his son could meet the same fate as singer Sidhu Moosewala, who was assassinated in Punjab in 2022. The last two years have been traumatic for Salman Khan, who has drastically cut down on his public appearances. Shetty’s life has been circumscribed since shots were fired at his house in Juhu in February this year. His set for ‘Golmaal-5’, helmed by Ajay Devgn, was as secure as Fort Knox (a major US Army installation in Kentucky), said an actor who worked on the film. “We created a bubble around Rohit. There were no outsiders allowed, and other than the actors and the senior technical team, no one was allowed close to him. His security was iron-clad,” said a wardrobe assistant who worked on the film, describing the atmosphere on set as “extremely stressful.” A film producer said the industry had only a few years ago begun to emerge from the shadows of the 1990s when the writ of the Mumbai mafia ran unchecked. “Extortions, forcible casting, shootouts, killings…that had all stopped in the last few years, and we thought the worst was behind us. But it seems to be changing. My antenna went up when I heard that they [Bishnoi gang members] asked Ranveer Singh to pay extortion money after the success of ‘Dhurandhar’. That kind of thing makes us all vulnerable. Our high profile makes us soft targets, and we have little assurance from the administration or the police.” People aware of the matter said that Mumbai Police have not received any complaints of extortion from anyone in the film industry so far.

news.headline: AISA president Neha Bora moves Delhi HC, challenges police notice to execute bond
news.story_lead: AISA president Neha Bora moves Delhi HC, challenges police notice to execute bond In her petition, Neha Bora said the SEM’s notice was prima facie ambiguous, factually incorrect and violates Articles 19 and 21 of the Constitution. All India Students’ Association (AISA) president Neha Bora on Monday moved the Delhi high court, challenging a police notice directing her to furnish a personal bond of ₹ 10,000, along with one surety, to “maintain peace during the period of inquiry” following her participation in a flag march. A New Delhi district police officer, designated as the Special Executive Magistrate (SEM), directed her to appear before it on Monday and execute a bond.
news.full_article_text: AISA president Neha Bora moves Delhi HC, challenges police notice to execute bond In her petition, Neha Bora said the SEM’s notice was prima facie ambiguous, factually incorrect and violates Articles 19 and 21 of the Constitution. All India Students’ Association (AISA) president Neha Bora on Monday moved the Delhi high court, challenging a police notice directing her to furnish a personal bond of ₹ 10,000, along with one surety, to “maintain peace during the period of inquiry” following her participation in a flag march. A New Delhi district police officer, designated as the Special Executive Magistrate (SEM), directed her to appear before it on Monday and execute a bond. The order was issued on October 17 (Saturday), the same day she was released after being detained on Friday for participating in the flag march. Also Read | AISA's Neha Bora released, CJP's Abhijeet Dipke arrested; police to file 7-8 FIRs amid anti-EC stir Bora challenges ₹ 10,000 bond notice in Delhi HC The notice cited three grounds for requiring her to execute the bond: alleged sloganeering at Mandi House on October 16; repeated protests in the vicinity of Jantar Mantar despite prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS); and the allegation that, on October 16, she instigated people to participate in a protest at Connaught Place. In her petition filed through advocate Abhik Chimni, Bora said the notice was prima facie ambiguous, factually incorrect and violates Articles 19 and 21 of the Constitution. The notice does not produce any material or information to substantiate the “likelihood” of breach of peace, fails to disclose the period, occasion or event in relation to which a breach is apprehended, the petition said. news.headline: CISF personnel nabs man attempting to flee Delhi's Jama Masjid metro station after suspicious object spotted during checking
news.story_lead: CISF personnel nabs man attempting to flee Delhi's Jama Masjid metro station after suspicious object spotted during checking The passenger, who claimed to be an NRI residing in Kuala Lumpur, was apprehended near the exit gate, the CISF said in a post on X. Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) personnel apprehended a passenger at Delhi's Jama Masjid Metro Station on Saturday, October 17, after he allegedly attempted to flee when a suspicious object appeared on the X-ray baggage inspection system screen (XBIS) On investigation, Delhi Police recovered around 155 grams of a gold powder-like substance concealed in an undergarment, news agency ANI reported. The man, identified as Mohd.
news.full_article_text: CISF personnel nabs man attempting to flee Delhi's Jama Masjid metro station after suspicious object spotted during checking The passenger, who claimed to be an NRI residing in Kuala Lumpur, was apprehended near the exit gate, the CISF said in a post on X. Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) personnel apprehended a passenger at Delhi's Jama Masjid Metro Station on Saturday, October 17, after he allegedly attempted to flee when a suspicious object appeared on the X-ray baggage inspection system screen (XBIS) On investigation, Delhi Police recovered around 155 grams of a gold powder-like substance concealed in an undergarment, news agency ANI reported. The man, identified as Mohd. Shuaib, a resident of Muzaffarnagar in Uttar Pradesh who also disclosed an address in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, was handed over to the police for further investigation. This comes after CISF personnel noticed a suspicious, dense object on the XBIS screen. The passenger allegedly attempted to flee and was apprehended near the exit gate. “Alert CISF personnel at Jama Masjid Metro Station of DMRC sprang into action when a passenger attempted to flee after a suspicious, dense object appeared on the XBIS screen during baggage screening," it said in a post on X on Monday. “Demonstrating quick reflexes and effective coordination, CISF personnel immediately pursued and apprehended the fleeing passenger near the exit gate,” it added. Also Read: AISA president Neha Bora moves Delhi HC, challenges police notice to execute bond In a video released by the CRPF, the passenger is seen talking on the phone before attempting to flee the station via an escalator towards the exit. A CRPF personnel is seen taking the stairs, reaching the top before the passenger and apprehending him. What investigation revealed Police said it received a call on October 17 about a person apprehended by CISF personnel. ASI Masum Raza, who was on patrolling duty, reached the spot and took custody of Shuaib. During an examination of his belongings, a gold powder-like substance weighing approximately 155 grams was found concealed inside an undergarment kept in his backpack, police said, according to ANI. Shuaib told police that he lived in Malaysia and worked in the textile sector. He said he had arrived in Delhi on October 16 with the substance and stayed at a hotel in the Jama Masjid area. He was detained at Jama Masjid Metro Station while heading to Lajpat Nagar. As police suspected that the recovered substance could be a narcotic or psychotropic substance, the concerned Narcotics Department was contacted for examination. The substance was subsequently found not to be a narcotic, police said. Police said Shuaib failed to provide documents proving ownership of the substance or a satisfactory explanation for possessing it. Legal proceedings were subsequently initiated against him under the Delhi Police Act at the Supreme Court Metro Police Station. news.headline: Keeping up with UP: Can Rahul Gandhi’s street activism revive the Congress in UP?
news.story_lead: Keeping up with UP: Can Rahul Gandhi’s street activism revive the Congress in UP? Can the Congress or its cadre in Uttar Pradesh amplify Rahul Gandhi's combative mood or remain bogged down with internecine troubles? On the day Congress leader Rahul Gandhi was protesting in the streets of Delhi, belligerently raising the public issue of ‘vote chori’, Congressmen in Lucknow publicly exchanged blows, seemingly over organisational changes, at the party headquarters.
news.full_article_text: Keeping up with UP: Can Rahul Gandhi’s street activism revive the Congress in UP? Can the Congress or its cadre in Uttar Pradesh amplify Rahul Gandhi's combative mood or remain bogged down with internecine troubles? On the day Congress leader Rahul Gandhi was protesting in the streets of Delhi, belligerently raising the public issue of ‘vote chori’, Congressmen in Lucknow publicly exchanged blows, seemingly over organisational changes, at the party headquarters. That their leader was being battered and bruised did not worry them. Nor did the fact that the crucial assembly elections are coming up and the party’s prospects remained seemingly dismal. Watching with dismay were senior Congress leaders, including the party deputy leader in the Rajya Sabha, Pramod Tiwari, and his MLA daughter, Aradhana Mishra, the newly elected Uttar Pradesh Congress Committee (UPCC) president. It was her first day in office. Significantly, the scuffle involved the outgoing firebrand president Ajay Rai and a lesser-known woman corporator. The ugly scenes in the party office literally threw cold water on the hard work of their leader, whose various street strategies have evoked hopes but have yet to generate votes – remember, Congress has lost Bihar and UP looks distant. The reasons are many, including the image of a naïve politician the BJP has built of Rahul Gandhi Gandhi’s public image has perceptibly improved, even though Modi supporters lose no opportunity to ridicule him for his political naivety. The old narrative that started from the times of the country's first prime minister, ‘After Nehru, who?’ or the perennial TINA (There Is No Alternative), remains in the air in favour of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. But can the Congress or its cadre in Uttar Pradesh amplify his combative mood or remain bogged down with internecine troubles? Infighting is not new to Congress; rather, it persists in every political party from top to bottom. Congress' history of infighting Old Congressmen recall the days of Kamlapati Tripathi vs Chandra Bhanu Gupta who despite their internal rivalry often cooperated strategically to engineer the downfall of their common rival like Sampurnanand. Later, the party infighting took a caste hue with the emergence of Rajput leadership in the 1980s and for several decades, it remained infested with a Brahmin vs Rajput one-upmanship war. Sanjay Singh, the titular Raja of Amethi, was tipped to be the chief minister in 1980, but after much celebration, he was dropped in favour of another Rajput Vishwanath Pratap Singh, who went on to become India’s seventh prime minister. Singh launched both the Bofors campaign against Rajiv Gandhi and the Mandal initiative, granting quotas for the OBCs. Congress leaders fought with each other -- Kamlapati Tripathi’s family from Varanasi vs Vir Bahadur Singh from Gorakhpur, ND Tiwari vs Vir Bahadur Singh, et al. Even Sripati Mishra, who replaced Vishwanath Pratap Singh in 1982, faced furious dissidence during his three-year tenure. While they were stalwarts who were remote-controlled by Delhi, here a corporator was taking on an outgoing state chief of the party, Ajay Rai, who, irrespective of his temperament, had travelled the state extensively to galvanise the party. He not only gave a spirited fight against the country's PM in the Varanasi Lok Sabha constituency in 2024, but the party's overall tally also improved under his leadership. The organisational changes in the Congress, made on the eve of elections, were also apparently triggered by the infighting that continues to plague the party. The former AICC general secretary in charge of UP affairs, Avinash Pandey, and Ajay Rai had teamed up well. But soon after Pandey was replaced by Rajendra Pal Gautam, a prominent Dalit leader, speculation started about Rai's removal. Rai’s family was in Congress, but he had started his political career in the BJP. He wore a vermilion tikka on his forehead and frequently visited temples. Gautam came from AAP via BSP and visited Sarnath during his trip to Varanasi. Political experts believe the Congress high command erred by implementing organisational changes just ahead of the elections. Though Rahul Gandhi spoke to Rai before the announcement, Rai perhaps felt humiliated. Undoubtedly, he is a strongman with muscle and money power, but he kept waiting for Delhi to appoint his organisational team. The soft-spoken, newly appointed chief, Mishra, also needs time to win the party's confidence and galvanise it for the polls. news.exam_corner_topic: Beyond fighter jets: What India needs to prepare for the wars of tomorrow
news.headline: Beyond fighter jets: What India needs to prepare for the wars of tomorrow
news.story_lead: Beyond fighter jets: What India needs to prepare for the wars of tomorrow In a conversation with HT Senior Anchor Aayesha Varma on Point Blank, Executive Editor Shishir Gupta argued that India must look beyond fleet numbers. India’s airpower debate is no longer simply about how many fighter jets the country needs. It is about what those aircraft can achieve in skies increasingly threatened by long-range missiles, drones and sophisticated air defences.
news.full_article_text: Beyond fighter jets: What India needs to prepare for the wars of tomorrow In a conversation with HT Senior Anchor Aayesha Varma on Point Blank, Executive Editor Shishir Gupta argued that India must look beyond fleet numbers. India’s airpower debate is no longer simply about how many fighter jets the country needs. It is about what those aircraft can achieve in skies increasingly threatened by long-range missiles, drones and sophisticated air defences. In a conversation with Hindustan Times Senior Anchor Aayesha Varma on Point Blank, Executive Editor Shishir Gupta argued that India must look beyond fleet numbers. More fighters remain necessary, but they must form part of a wider military capability combining unmanned systems, longer-range weapons and layered defences. The central objective is deterrence: preventing an adversary from attacking by making the likely costs unacceptably high. More fighters, but not numbers alone The discussion began with Air Chief Marshal A.P. Singh’s call to induct 38–40 fighters annually as the Indian Air Force seeks to rebuild its declining strength. Gupta said the fleet had fallen below 30 squadrons, against a benchmark of approximately 42.5. He also drew a distinction over that benchmark, saying it had been authorised by the Chairman, Chiefs of Staff Committee, rather than the Cabinet Committee on Security. Yet the numerical shortfall tells only part of the story. Gupta questioned whether adding aircraft, without improving the weapons they carry, would deliver sufficient military advantage. His argument centred on standoff weapons: missiles and other munitions that allow aircraft to strike from farther away, reducing their exposure to hostile air defences. A larger fighter fleet becomes more useful when its aircraft can attack without having to fly deep into an adversary’s defensive envelope. Why range changes the equation For Gupta, the priority is not choosing between aircraft and missiles, but ensuring they work together. Longer-range air-to-air weapons can threaten enemy aircraft at greater distances. Air-to-ground weapons can allow pilots to attack targets while remaining farther from defensive systems. The same logic, he argued, should influence where India stations its aircraft, with attention to protecting bases from enemy strikes. He also cautioned against viewing India’s requirements primarily through Pakistan. China, he said, must shape the longer-term assessment of the scale and sophistication of the threat. That shifts the question from “How many fighters are enough?” to something more demanding: what combination of aircraft, weapons and protected infrastructure can remain effective against a powerful adversary? Also Read | Does India need stand-off missiles or more fighter jets? What drone warfare does - and does not - prove Gupta pointed to Ukraine, Iran and the Houthis to illustrate how forces with limited conventional airpower can use missiles and drones to impose costs on stronger opponents. In his assessment, attacks on infrastructure demonstrate that military pressure need not depend entirely on a large fighter fleet. Relatively inexpensive weapons can also create an uncomfortable economic imbalance when defenders use costly interceptors against them. But he stopped short of arguing that India should abandon manned aircraft. India, he said, has too much at stake to rely exclusively on drones, loitering munitions or missiles. The lesson is therefore not that fighters have become irrelevant. It is that they cannot be expected to deliver every military objective by themselves. Gupta’s preferred approach combines manned and unmanned capabilities according to the target, the adversary and the intended outcome. Also Read | ‘Delay in inducting new fighter jets hurting IAF’: Air Chief Marshal AP Singh highlights need for strengthening IAF A shield must match the threat The discussion also highlighted the importance of defending against the weapons transforming offensive warfare. Gupta argued that India needs a layered response rather than a single, all-purpose shield. Different threats require different interception options, particularly when the cost of destroying a cheap drone can far exceed the cost of launching it. He discussed systems ranging from lower-level interception capabilities to Akash and the S-400, alongside indigenous interceptor development. His broader point was that defensive planning must account for both effectiveness and affordability. The stakes extend beyond military installations. Gupta linked protection against missile attacks to civilian morale and economic confidence. In that framing, air and missile defence are not merely supporting capabilities; they help preserve the stability on which national growth depends. Also Read | ‘Definitely no’: Ex-Air Force vice chief questions relevance of Tejas Mk-2 fighter jets in mid 2030s, slams HAL delay Building reach around existing aircraft Gupta identified several weapons programmes as important to strengthening India’s existing and future aircraft. These included work on a lighter BrahMos missile for smaller fighters, the Rudram anti-radiation missile programme and longer-range Astra air-to-air missiles. He presented them as complementary efforts to extend striking power and expand the distances at which India can threaten hostile aircraft or engage targets. The underlying procurement argument is significant: improving the weapons available to a fighter can be as important as acquiring the aircraft itself. He also placed airpower within a wider deterrence framework that includes conventional missiles, submarines and underwater drones. The emphasis was on building multiple military options rather than making one platform responsible for national security. The fifth-generation fighter dilemma That same reasoning shaped Gupta’s assessment of fifth-generation aircraft. He acknowledged the value of advanced fighters and discussed stealth features such as carrying weapons internally to reduce radar visibility. But he rejected the idea that acquiring such aircraft would, by itself, resolve India’s security challenges. With a finite defence budget, expensive fighters must be weighed against other requirements, including unmanned combat systems and missile defence. Gupta’s central prescription was a balanced force: advanced aircraft where they add decisive value, longer-range weapons to improve their effectiveness, unmanned systems to broaden operational choices, and defences that protect the country against retaliation. The challenge is not to buy every available capability, but to build a combination that can achieve India’s military objectives. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Shishir Gupta Shishir Gupta is Executive Editor at Hindustan Times and one of India's top journalists covering national security, strategic affairs, foreign policy and geopolitics. news.headline: Shooters planned to kill Tiger Shroff in Mumbai, motive unclear, say police
news.story_lead: Shooters planned to kill Tiger Shroff in Mumbai, motive unclear, say police DCP added that the motive behind the attack had not yet been ascertained and would become clear after the interrogation of the suspected assailants. Police believe the shooters who opened fire at actor Tiger Shroff’s car in Mumbai intended to kill him, though the motive behind the attack remains unclear, Deputy Commissioner of Police Raj Tilak Roushan said on Monday. “The manner in which the firing was carried out suggests that the intention was to kill,” DCP Roushan said at a press conference.
news.full_article_text: Shooters planned to kill Tiger Shroff in Mumbai, motive unclear, say police DCP added that the motive behind the attack had not yet been ascertained and would become clear after the interrogation of the suspected assailants. Police believe the shooters who opened fire at actor Tiger Shroff’s car in Mumbai intended to kill him, though the motive behind the attack remains unclear, Deputy Commissioner of Police Raj Tilak Roushan said on Monday. “The manner in which the firing was carried out suggests that the intention was to kill,” DCP Roushan said at a press conference. He added that the motive behind the attack had not yet been ascertained and would become clear after the interrogation of the suspected assailants. Also Read | Tiger Shroff attack: How Lawrence Bishnoi gang’s overseas network operates Five to six rounds were fired They also said that none of the three accused arrested in connection with the firing at actor Tiger Shroff’s car was a minor. The police also said that two of the three accused had fired five to six rounds at the actor’s car during the incident. Addressing a press conference, Deputy Commissioner of Police Raj Tilak Roushan said that one of the arrested accused is 18 years old, while the other two are 22 years old. "Two accused are from Haryana, and one is from Bihar. Two of the three arrested assailants had fired five to six rounds at Tiger Shroff's car," he said. Also Read | Tiger Shroff attack suspects caught in Kota, had received ₹ 50,000 in advance: Police Accused's motorcyle found in Mumbai Roushan further said that the motorcycle allegedly used by the accused in the firing incident had been found in Mumbai’s Andheri area. However, the police had not recovered any weapon from the three suspects so far. "No weapon was recovered from three suspects. We are bringing them to Mumbai from Rajasthan," he said. The DCP also said that the police had not received any prior complaint regarding a threat to Tiger Shroff before the firing incident. "The motive behind firing on the actor is not yet ascertained. We will find it out after interrogating the suspected assailants," the DCP added. news.headline: CJP leaders Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka’s judicial custody extended by two days; Delhi Police cite ‘peace, tranquillity’ concerns
news.story_lead: CJP leaders Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka’s judicial custody extended by two days; Delhi Police cite ‘peace, tranquillity’ concerns Delhi Police had sought further custody of the duo, claiming their release could disrupt “peace and tranquility.” A Special Executive Magistrate (SEM) on Monday extended the judicial custody of Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka by two days over allegations that they breached security and entered Jantar Mantar during protests against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Delhi Police had sought further custody of the duo, claiming their release could disrupt “peace and tranquility.” Follow LIVE updates here. However, CJP’s legal team countered the apprehension, arguing that there was not an iota of evidence to suggest that the duo posed any threat or that their release would disturb public order.

news.headline: Indian embassy in Italy issues advisory, urges citizens to avoid protest sites, crowded areas
news.story_lead: Indian embassy in Italy issues advisory, urges citizens to avoid protest sites, crowded areas The advisory comes amid unrest in parts of Italy over poor public services and the rising cost of living. The Indian embassy in Italy has issued a safety advisory for Indian nationals amid protests over rising living costs and poor public services, some of which turned violent over the weekend. The embassy has urged Indians to avoid crowded areas and protest sites, exercise caution and follow local news for updates.
news.full_article_text: Indian embassy in Italy issues advisory, urges citizens to avoid protest sites, crowded areas The advisory comes amid unrest in parts of Italy over poor public services and the rising cost of living. The Indian embassy in Italy has issued a safety advisory for Indian nationals amid protests over rising living costs and poor public services, some of which turned violent over the weekend. The embassy has urged Indians to avoid crowded areas and protest sites, exercise caution and follow local news for updates. “Indian nationals are advised to exercise caution, avoid crowded areas and locations where protests are taking place, and follow local news about such events,” the advisory released on Monday said. “In case of any emergency, Indian nationals can contact the Embassy of India in Rome at +39 331 614 2085 or the Consulate General of India in Milan at +39 3881647527,” it added. Also Read | From France to Italy: Looting, vandalism prevails across Europe as rising cost of living stirs unrest Italy protests: Police clash with demonstrators in Milan The advisory comes after Milan police clashed with protesters throwing stones and looting shops during demonstrations against poor services and the rising cost of living on Sunday. The clashes followed similar unrest in several Italian cities a day earlier. Police in riot gear fired tear gas and used water cannons after several hundred hooded protesters broke shop windows and set bins on fire in the area near central Piazza Duomo, sources with knowledge of the investigation told Reuters. The demonstrations escalated as protesters engaged in acts of vandalism, prompting police to intervene to disperse the crowds and restore order in the area. More than 60 protesters were taken to the police station for further checks, the sources added. Also Read | Milan Unrest: Police Clash With Protesters as Tear Gas and Water Cannons Deployed on Day 2 28 arrested after clashes in northern Italian cities A total of 28 protesters were arrested after similar clashes erupted on Saturday in northern cities, including Milan, Bologna, Brescia, Bergamo and Turin, according to a police report on Sunday. The incidents across multiple cities highlighted growing public discontent over the cost of living and the quality of public services. The demonstrations also prompted security concerns as some gatherings descended into violence. The developments come as authorities deal with unrest linked to economic pressures and dissatisfaction with public services, with police intervening in several locations over the weekend. Italy protests echo unrest in neighbouring France The clashes in Italy echoed the violence in neighbouring France, where hundreds of thousands of people angered by rising costs and declining public services took to the streets on Saturday in some of the country's most violent protests in years. The demonstrations in France reflected wider public anger over economic pressures and concerns about the availability and quality of essential public services. The unrest also underscored the challenges facing authorities as people take to the streets to express their grievances. Giorgia Meloni condemns violence, calls government meeting Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, who is facing an election next year, condemned the violence and announced a government meeting on Monday to discuss how to address the situation. The meeting is expected to focus on the response to the unrest and measures to deal with the issues contributing to the demonstrations. news.headline: On camera, Tiger Shroff shooting suspects seen rushing to catch train in Surat before arrest in Kota
news.story_lead: On camera, Tiger Shroff shooting suspects seen rushing to catch train in Surat before arrest in Kota The three suspects were nabbed on Monday from Rajasthan's Kota from where they were planning to flee to Nepal via Delhi. Fresh details have emerged in the shooting case involving Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff, with CCTV footage from Surat railway station helping police track down the three alleged assailants, who were arrested in Rajasthan’s Kota on Monday. Shroff escaped unhurt after three motorcycle-borne assailants opened fire at him in Mumbai on Sunday evening as he was leaving a club in his car after playing football.
news.full_article_text: On camera, Tiger Shroff shooting suspects seen rushing to catch train in Surat before arrest in Kota The three suspects were nabbed on Monday from Rajasthan's Kota from where they were planning to flee to Nepal via Delhi. Fresh details have emerged in the shooting case involving Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff, with CCTV footage from Surat railway station helping police track down the three alleged assailants, who were arrested in Rajasthan’s Kota on Monday. Shroff escaped unhurt after three motorcycle-borne assailants opened fire at him in Mumbai on Sunday evening as he was leaving a club in his car after playing football. The suspects subsequently travelled by road from Mumbai to Surat, where they boarded the Pune-Jaipur Express (train 12939). They were arrested in Kota on Monday morning while allegedly attempting to flee to Nepal via Delhi . Also read: Shooters planned to kill Tiger Shroff in Mumbai, motive unclear, say police According to railway officials, a team of Railway Police Force (RPF) and Government Railway Police (GRP) was formed based on inputs received from the police. "The surveillance footage was checked at various stations after which they were tracked from Surat railway station. The team of rail police along with local police apprehended them at Kota the next day, at around 10.15 am," said a Western Railway official. Fresh clip shows men rushing to catch train Deep Dive Two CCTV footages seen by HT show the trio rushing their way to catch the train. Two of the three men are dressed in white shirts, while the third one is seen wearing a blue T-shirt, carrying a bag. They can be seen walking hurriedly outside the station. On the platform, the trio is seen rushing past the crowd to catch the train – two running ahead and the third one closely following behind. The CCTV footages became a crucial piece of evidence for the cops who were trying to nab the assailants in the high-profile case. How investigators tracked the assailants The three suspects were detained from the general coach of the Pune-Jaipur Express when the train arrived at Kota railway station. According to the RPF, Kota division received information from the Mumbai Police crime branch about the suspects travelling on the train in connection with the firing incident in Juhu. "The joint team checked the train upon its arrival and detained the three men before they could proceed further. Preliminary information indicated that the suspects had travelled by road from Mumbai to Surat before boarding the train," said the railway official. Who are the assailants? The suspects have been identified as Rehan alias Sukka (18), a resident of Sonipat in Haryana; Ritwik Kurmi alias Roshan Fighter (22), reportedly from Bihar and currently residing in Andheri West. While the third suspect was initially said to be a minor, the cops later clarified that all the three men are adults – the third one identified as 18-years-old-Phool Singh. One of the accused is said to be a driver working for app based aggregator Rapido.
