news.headline: Uttarakhand minister confronts Daler Mehndi on stage, alleges singer was drinking alcohol: ‘You cannot even speak’
news.story_lead: Uttarakhand minister confronts Daler Mehndi on stage, alleges singer was drinking alcohol: ‘You cannot even speak’ A video of the incident has surfaced on social media, showing Uniyal standing on the stage while Mehndi stood beside him. Singer Daler Mehndi's performance at a fair in Uttarakhand was interrupted by state cabinet minister Subodh Uniyal, who took to the stage to confront the singer reportedly over alcohol consumption during the show. A purported video of the incident has surfaced on social media, showing Uniyal standing on the stage while Mehndi stood beside him.
news.full_article_text: Uttarakhand minister confronts Daler Mehndi on stage, alleges singer was drinking alcohol: ‘You cannot even speak’ A video of the incident has surfaced on social media, showing Uniyal standing on the stage while Mehndi stood beside him. Singer Daler Mehndi's performance at a fair in Uttarakhand was interrupted by state cabinet minister Subodh Uniyal, who took to the stage to confront the singer reportedly over alcohol consumption during the show. A purported video of the incident has surfaced on social media, showing Uniyal standing on the stage while Mehndi stood beside him. Also Read | Bihar: Viral video shows three women, man consuming liquor inside Darbhanga hospital; police probe underway The controversy erupted during the cultural evening of the historic 'Siddhpeeth Maa Kunjapuri Tourism and Development Fair' in Uttarakhand's New Tehri on Sunday night, according to news agency PTI . The Kunjapuri fair is a significant event rooted in religious faith and cultural traditions. 'You cannot even speak': Minister to Mehndi The issue began with questions over whether the singer was performing live or relying on a background soundtrack. During the programme, the minister objected to the singer's performance and was heard saying, "You cannot even speak, so how are you going to sing?" Addressing the singer on stage, Narendra Nagar MLA Uniyal remarked that the audience had come to hear him perform and that he was therefore expected to meet the standards they anticipated. He also stressed the importance of maintaining decorum, noting that the event was taking place during the religious period of Navratri. In the viral footage, Uniyal further criticised the performance, saying, "We called you so that our people could be entertained. You are making a fool of us." The minister alleged that the singer was inebriated; however, the allegations could not be confirmed, the report stated. Also Read | Social media user booked over posts questioning Uttarakhand Global Investors Summit "This is wrong. It's wrong. You have a big name; we should respect that. You were called because you have a big name," Uniyal said. Meanwhile, Mehndi requested the minister to leave the stage. The video of the incident was widely shared by social media users. However, HT could not independently verify the authenticity of the video. Meanwhile, some of his more recent works include the title track of the 2016 film 'Dangal'. news.headline: CJP's Abhijeet Dipke targets PM Modi over extended custody of Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka
news.story_lead: CJP's Abhijeet Dipke targets PM Modi over extended custody of Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka "Ashu and Saurav’s first crime was waving the Tiranga at Jantar Mantar. Their second crime? Refusing to back down," Abhijeet Dipke said in a post on X.
news.full_article_text: CJP's Abhijeet Dipke targets PM Modi over extended custody of Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka "Ashu and Saurav’s first crime was waving the Tiranga at Jantar Mantar. Their second crime? Refusing to back down," Abhijeet Dipke said in a post on X. Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Monday said party co-convenors Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka remained undeterred despite spending five days in jail, claiming they walked into court with smiles on their faces and their spirits unbroken. Das and Ranka were sent to judicial remand for another two days after being produced before a newly appointed Special Executive Magistrate (SEM) at Mandir Marg police station, an official said. "Ashu and Saurav’s first crime was waving the Tiranga at Jantar Mantar. Their second crime? Refusing to back down. Even after five days in jail, they walked into court with smiles on their faces, their spirits unbroken," Dipke said in a post on X. Deep Dive The two were initially sent to five-day judicial custody on October 13 after allegedly climbing over a locked gate to enter Jantar Mantar, which had earlier been denotified as a designated protest site. Also Read | CJP leaders Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka’s judicial custody extended by two days; Delhi Police cite ‘peace, tranquillity’ concerns Dipke targets PM Modi over detention In a lengthy Instagram post, Dipke accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi of using the state machinery to intimidate young protesters and suppress dissent. He questioned the government's decision to keep 26-27-year-old Saurav Das and 30-year-old Ashutosh Ranka in custody for waving the Tricolour at Jantar Mantar. "The great Vishwaguru Narendra Modi must be feeling very strong keeping 26-27-year-old Saurabh Das in jail and keeping 30-year-old Ashutosh behind bars. This is what strength looks like? Hiding behind the police, hiding behind the courts—is this Narendra Modi's strength?" he said. Dipke alleged that the duo had been denied timely hearings, with proceedings repeatedly postponed. He accused Modi of projecting strength by keeping young protesters behind bars and deploying the police and security forces against those opposing his government. Describing the two leaders' conduct in court as an example of courage, Dipke said Das had walked in with a smile even after spending five days in jail and learning that his judicial custody had been extended. He recalled that Das had once told him he would not be able to endure even a day in jail, but had remained composed despite spending five days in custody. "Real strength is knowing that you are fighting a power much greater than yourself. It is knowing what the consequences could be and still refusing to remain silent," he said. Dipke also recounted speaking to Das's mother, saying she remained confident that her son would not break despite being in jail. He said the resolve shown by the families of both leaders reflected the courage that the government had failed to intimidate. He said the continued detention of the two leaders would inspire more young people to speak out rather than deter them from protesting. Follow here for live udpates CJP alleges delay in bail proceedings The CJP has alleged that bail proceedings were deliberately delayed to prevent the release of its two co-convenors. Along with other party workers, Das and Ranka had displayed the national flag at Jantar Mantar and raised slogans against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar before being detained and placed under preventive arrest. On Sunday, the Special Executive Magistrate hearing their bail matter claimed that unknown persons were threatening him, following which police registered a non-cognisable report. In a post on X, Dipke alleged that the authorities were using delays to prolong the duo's detention. "The state is deliberately prolonging Ashu and Saurav's illegal arrest by using every dirty trick in the book to delay court proceedings and prevent their release. news.exam_corner_topic: Security tightened for Dussehra in Delhi-NCR, crowd management and traffic plan in place
news.headline: Security tightened for Dussehra in Delhi-NCR, crowd management and traffic plan in place
news.story_lead: Security tightened for Dussehra in Delhi-NCR, crowd management and traffic plan in place Elaborate security arrangements with 1,200 police personnel have also been made in Faridabad to maintain law and order. Over 13,000 police personnel will be deployed across Delhi-NCR to ensure tight security during Dussehra celebrations, with heightened vigilance at religious sites and places expected to see large public gatherings, officers said. Around 2,200 police personnel have been deployed at 66 'Ravan Dahan' sites, 17 religious processions and other related events in Gurugram, with police making extensive security arrangements for Dussehra on Tuesday.
news.full_article_text: Security tightened for Dussehra in Delhi-NCR, crowd management and traffic plan in place Elaborate security arrangements with 1,200 police personnel have also been made in Faridabad to maintain law and order. Over 13,000 police personnel will be deployed across Delhi-NCR to ensure tight security during Dussehra celebrations, with heightened vigilance at religious sites and places expected to see large public gatherings, officers said. Around 2,200 police personnel have been deployed at 66 'Ravan Dahan' sites, 17 religious processions and other related events in Gurugram, with police making extensive security arrangements for Dussehra on Tuesday. Traffic police have also prepared plans for smooth crowd management. Delhi Police said its personnel will be deployed round the clock at sensitive locations, while senior officers will inspect deployment sites to review security arrangements and ensure adequate manpower. Around 10,000 police personnel will be deployed across Delhi for Dussehra, it said. Also Read | No illegal detention of protesters in Delhi; metro, internet to run normally orders Supreme Court Special attention will be given to crowded areas, prominent temples, pandals and venues where Dussehra events are organised, as authorities expect a significant footfall during the celebrations. Additional Deputy Commissioner of Central District, Angad Mehta, said the district experiences a substantial increase in footfall during the festive season, requiring extensive security arrangements. "The Central District experiences a very heavy load during the festive season. Beyond Dussehra, we also see a significant footfall at Jhandewalan during Navratri. Furthermore, Durga Puja celebrations are currently underway simultaneously at multiple locations," Mehta said. "Consequently, the Central District has put comprehensive arrangements in place, with police personnel, both male and female, deployed around the clock. Senior officers also conduct regular visits to the deployment sites. In light of this, we have ensured the deployment of an adequate police force," he added. Police officers said security personnel would be positioned at strategic locations to manage crowds, maintain law and order and respond swiftly to any emergency during the festivities. The deployment will also focus on preventing pickpocketing, snatching and other street crimes that tend to pose a challenge in crowded areas during major festivals. Police teams will remain alert to any suspicious activity, officers said. Crowd management and traffic regulation will be key components of the security plan, particularly around major religious sites and venues hosting Dussehra events. Police personnel will coordinate with other agencies to ensure the smooth movement of devotees and visitors. Senior officers will monitor the arrangements and assess requirements at different locations, with additional personnel to be deployed wherever necessary, they said. Police have urged people to remain vigilant, follow instructions issued by security personnel and immediately report any suspicious object or activity to the nearest police officer. In Gurugram, police additional police personnel have been deployed at major venues, keeping in mind the size of the expected crowd. Police have identified 12 major and 54 small Ravan Dahan venues. Sixteen sites fall under the East Zone, 23 under the West Zone, seven under the South Zone and 20 under the Manesar Zone. The responsibilities of designated police officers and personnel have been clearly assigned at each site to ensure effective crowd control, security monitoring and maintenance of law and order. Special security arrangements have also been made for religious processions to be taken out across the district during Dussehra. Police personnel have been deployed for three processions in the East Zone, nine in the West Zone, two in the South Zone and three in the Manesar Zone, they added. One fire tender, one ambulance and one duty magistrate will be deployed at each of the 12 major Ravan Dahan sites. In addition, two fire tenders and two ambulances will remain on standby in each police zone to provide immediate assistance in case of an emergency, police said. In view of the anticipated increase in traffic around event venues during Dussehra, the traffic police will implement special traffic management measures. A separate, detailed duty roster has been issued for traffic and parking management, with dedicated personnel deployed accordingly, they added. "Special arrangements have been made to ensure public safety, facilitate smooth crowd management, maintain traffic discipline and respond effectively to any emergency situation with additional security arrangements. "In addition, one Quick Response Team (QRT) has been arranged for each police zone. To strengthen security at Dussehra fairs and other public events, special attention will be given to surveillance, public address systems, security checks and emergency response measures," A Gurugram Police spokesperson said. In Faridabad, special surveillance will be maintained at event venues, markets, major thoroughfares, and crowded areas. All concerned officers and Station House Officers (SHOs) have been directed to monitor security arrangements in their respective areas and maintain coordination with the organising committees, a Faridabad Police spokesperson said.

news.headline: British tourist sexually harassed in Kerala's Varkala, dress torn, video helps police arrest man

A British woman tourist was allegedly sexually harassed and had her dress torn by a man while returning to her room in Kerala’s Varkala around 1.30 am on Monday, police said.
news.full_article_text: British tourist sexually harassed in Kerala's Varkala, dress torn, video helps police arrest man The accused is expected to be produced before a court on Tuesday for remand. Further investigation is underway, police said. A British woman tourist was allegedly sexually harassed and had her dress torn by a man while returning to her room in Kerala’s Varkala around 1.30 am on Monday, police said. The accused, identified as Shahad, a resident of Odayam in Varkala, allegedly approached the woman as she was returning to her room after going out for food, and misbehaved with her before tearing her dress, police said, news agency PTI reported. The woman took refuge with a group of tourists, who intervened and stopped the accused. She approached the police on Monday morning, following which a case was registered. Police identified and arrested Shahad with the help of a video recorded by the woman. Meanwhile, in a separate case, a solo traveller currently hitchhiking across India shared an Instagram update about how her initial fears were dispelled by the kindness she encountered during her travels. Despite being warned about safety risks before arriving, the 24-year-old Portuguese creator, Ana, said that she experienced overwhelming helpfulness from people everywhere she went. “Before landing in India, everyone warned me about harassment, robbery, and stares. I was genuinely a bit afraid of going there and completely avoided hitchhiking for my entire first month in the country,” Ana wrote on Instagram. “But as time went by, the reality turned out to be completely different: Everywhere I went, I kept meeting the kindest, funniest, and most helpful people. From strangers on the street randomly spending two hours helping me fix a phone issue, to making lifelong friends—the men I met completely changed my perspective,” she added. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Karishma Ayaldasani Karishma Ayaldasani is a Senior Content Producer at Hindustan Times, based in New Delhi, where she works with the digital team on fast-moving breaking stories from India and around the world. news.story_lead: Court cites ‘habitualness’, ‘no respect for law’ in order extending CJP leaders' custody in Jantar Mantar trespassing case CJP termed the ‘preventive detention’ as ‘a complete mockery of legal process and said it will challenge the order before higher courts ‘immediately.’ A Special Executive Magistrate court said on Monday that Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das showed “no respect for law” as it extended their judicial custody by two days over the Jantar Mantar protest against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Citing the police investigation, the court order said the CJP leaders had “mobilized and enticed the general public” to gather and hold a protest at Jantar Mantar , which is no longer a designated protest site . The court on Monday rejected their sureties over allegations that they breached security and entered the site during
news.full_article_text: Court cites ‘habitualness’, ‘no respect for law’ in order extending CJP leaders' custody in Jantar Mantar trespassing case CJP termed the ‘preventive detention’ as ‘a complete mockery of legal process and said it will challenge the order before higher courts ‘immediately.’ A Special Executive Magistrate court said on Monday that Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das showed “no respect for law” as it extended their judicial custody by two days over the Jantar Mantar protest against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Citing the police investigation, the court order said the CJP leaders had “mobilized and enticed the general public” to gather and hold a protest at Jantar Mantar , which is no longer a designated protest site . The court on Monday rejected their sureties over allegations that they breached security and entered the site during the protest. “The IO further states that both the respondents are members of CJP and they mobilized and enticed the general public to assemble and stage protest at Jantar Mantar, which has been de-notified as a designated protest site,” the court order said, referring to the findings by Investigating Officer (IO). Deep Dive It further added that Ranka and Das, who are lodged in Tihar Jail, flouted their own undertaking of October 11, indicating ‘the apprehension to commit further offence’. The court, citing the police, said the arrested CJP leaders used social media to make repeated calls for protests at ‘non-designated sites such as Jantar Mantar and Connaught Place’. It also said the two CJP leaders were granted police permission to protest ‘on the basis of their assurance that they would strictly adhere to the terms of permission’. However, they failed to adhere to the terms, it said. Flagging that the two had shown no ‘respect for law’, the order said, “At this stage, the grounds of apprehension as presented before me apparently suggests that the conduct of the respondents is not above board; rather it shows no respect for law and their habitualness in calling protest at de-notified areas.” It also said the the CJP leaders' statements that they will not repeat the ‘offence’ in future ‘does not inspire confidence’ as it cited the police investigation in the Jantar Mantar trespassing case. “The application filed by IO is supported by substantial material on record, raising serious concerns regarding the likelihood of breach of peace and disturbance of public tranquility, which cannot be brushed aside without proper consideration,” it said. The Special Executive Magistrate Ritu Raj extended the judicial custody as he pointed out ‘imminent apprehension and past conduct’ of the two CJP leaders. He also said the sureties submitted by the defense counsel were ‘unfit to stand as surety’ , saying there was an ‘apparent mismatch’ of photographs in Bond and Aadhar card of surety. CJP responds to court order The CJP condemned the court proceeding in Ranka and Das' bail hearing and terming the ongoing preventive detention of party leaders ‘a complete mockery of legal process and state-sponsored overreach.’ The CJP termed the bail hearing a ‘farce' designed to ‘crush democratic voices’. "Our advocates spoke strictly on points of law , yet the authorities failed to present a single piece of evidence showing any threat to public peace," Ratna Singh, CJP's legal head, said. She also denied the allegation that a protest call was given by the youth-led movement for Das and Ranka's release after their judicial custody. The CJP in a statement said that when fresh sureties were produced with all required documentation and identity verifications, a fresh application seeking further judicial custody alleging an imminent threat to public order was filed. There was no factual basis or statement on record to support their claim, the CJP alleged. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Sana Fazili Sana started her career in 2018 with News18 and later moved to BoomLive. In the meantime, she thought it was a good idea to share what she learnt, hence took up part-time teaching of journalism course at Jamia Millia Islamia, which she says, she thoroughly enjoyed-not sure if the feeling was mutual. For a year, she also tried her hands at communication roles, only to realise she was more comfortable with news. So, joined HT in September 2025. Not much of a talker, always up for chai and sarcasm. And pun always intended. Her tag line is 'I will figure out, but I need to panic first' Read More - Cockroach Janta Party

news.exam_corner_topic: Houthi missile strike on Yemen camp kills 50 security recruits, local authorities say
news.headline: Houthi missile strike on Yemen camp kills 50 security recruits, local authorities say
news.story_lead: Yemen's government said the missile strike killed recruits to its internal security forces (file photo) - Published 2 hours ago More than 50 security personnel have been killed and 200 injured in a Houthi missile strike on a camp in Yemen's central province of Shabwa, local authorities say. A spokesman for the Saudi-backed Yemeni armed forces said the Iran-backed group launched three ballistic missiles at al-Alam camp near Ataq city, which was being used as a training centre for recruits to the security forces and police. The head of Yemen's Presidential Leadership Council, Rashad al-Alimi, condemned what he called the "criminal attack" and promised a "firm response".
news.full_article_text: Yemen's government said the missile strike killed recruits to its internal security forces (file photo) - Published 2 hours ago More than 50 security personnel have been killed and 200 injured in a Houthi missile strike on a camp in Yemen's central province of Shabwa, local authorities say. A spokesman for the Saudi-backed Yemeni armed forces said the Iran-backed group launched three ballistic missiles at al-Alam camp near Ataq city, which was being used as a training centre for recruits to the security forces and police. The head of Yemen's Presidential Leadership Council, Rashad al-Alimi, condemned what he called the "criminal attack" and promised a "firm response". The Houthis' military spokesman said they had targeted "Saudi enemy concentrations". Yemen's devastating civil war has flared up in recent months. At the start of October, pro-government forces launched a major offensive that aims to retake territory in western Yemen that is controlled by the Houthis. With air support from a Saudi-led coalition of Arab states, they managed to regain control of territory on the Red Sea coast that overlooks the strategically important Bab al-Mandab Strait, which the Houthis captured in a surprise assault in September. However, fierce fighting is continuing there, as well as around the besieged government-controlled city of Taiz, and to the north in Marib and al-Jawf provinces. The Houthis have also responded to the Saudi air strikes by launching missiles and drones at airports, energy facilities and military bases in neighbouring Saudi Arabia. - Houthi missile attack on Yemeni presidential palace kills five, minister says Published 3 days ago - On Yemen's desert battlefield, a war with global consequences is being waged Published 7 days ago - 'We are terrified but we want to get an education', say Yemeni schoolgirls Published 6 October Monday's attack in Shabwa is one of the deadliest reported since the start of the escalation. Shabwa province's media office said in a statement that ballistic missiles struck the Martyr Ahmed al-Sulaimani Training Centre, where recruits from several provinces were undergoing training to be members of the internal security forces. According to a preliminary assessment, 53 were killed and more than 200 injured, it added. A video posted on social media appeared to show several bodies scattered across the ground. Shabwa's deputy governor, Fahad al-Khalifi, told AFP news agency that hospitals in the province were overwhelmed and had been forced to transfer the most seriously wounded to neighbouring Hadramout and Aden, where the government is based. Some of them were in a critical condition, he said. Information Minister Moammar al-Eryani said the attack constituted a war crime because the internal security forces training centre was not a military target. He also accused the Houthis of "attempting to fabricate a false media victory, boost the morale of its collapsing elements, and cover up the defeats and setbacks it is suffering across various combat axes". The Houthis' military spokesman, Yahya Sarea, said in a statement that the missiles targeted a gathering of "Saudi enemy" forces at al-Alam camp, which he said was run by Saudi officers. There was no immediate comment from Saudi authorities. In a separate development, Houthi-run media reported that a Saudi air strike on a home in the Sahar district of the Houthi-controlled northern province of Saada on Sunday killed at least 10 people and injured 23 others, many of them women and children. According to the Houthi-run health ministry in north-western Yemen, a total of 141 people had been killed in Saudi strikes over the past seven weeks. The government's health ministry, meanwhile, said last week that at least 1,282 people had been killed in the conflict across Yemen since 6 August. In Saudi Arabia, at least 19 people have been killed in Houthi attacks targeting the kingdom's airports since the beginning of October. Yemen has been devastated by a civil war that began in 2014, when the Houthis ousted the government from the capital, Sanaa. The conflict escalated in 2015, after the Saudi-led coalition intervened in an attempt to restore the government's rule. A four-year-old informal ceasefire began to unravel in July, when the Houthis announced a "maritime embargo" against Saudi Arabia and began missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers in the Red Sea. The Houthis said they were retaliating for what they call a Saudi blockade of their territory, as well as an air strike on Sanaa airport that they blamed on the kingdom. Related topics

The Houthis have also responded to the Saudi air strikes by launching missiles and drones at airports, energy facilities and military bases in neighbouring Saudi Arabia. - Houthi missile attack on Yemeni presidential palace kills five, minister says Published 3 days ago - On Yemen's desert battlefield, a war with global consequences is being waged Published 7 days ago - 'We are terrified but we want to get an education', say Yemeni schoolgirls Published 6 October Monday's attack in Shabwa is one of the deadliest reported since the start of the escalation. Shabwa province's media office said in a statement that ballistic missiles struck the Martyr Ahmed al-Sulaimani Training Centre, where recruits from several provinces were undergoing training to be members of the internal security forces. According to a preliminary assessment, 53 were killed and more than 200 injured, it added. A video posted on social media appeared to show several bodies scattered across the ground. Shabwa's deputy governor, Fahad al-Khalifi, told AFP news agency that hospitals in the province were overwhelmed and had been forced to transfer the most seriously wounded to neighbouring Hadramout and Aden, where the government is based. Some of them were in a critical condition, he said. Information Minister Moammar al-Eryani said the attack constituted a war crime because the internal security forces training centre was not a military target. He also accused the Houthis of "attempting to fabricate a false media victory, boost the morale of its collapsing elements, and cover up the defeats and setbacks it is suffering across various combat axes". The Houthis' military spokesman, Yahya Sarea, said in a statement that the missiles targeted a gathering of "Saudi enemy" forces at al-Alam camp, which he said was run by Saudi officers. There was no immediate comment from Saudi authorities. In a separate development, Houthi-run media reported that a Saudi air strike on a home in the Sahar district of the Houthi-controlled northern province of Saada on Sunday killed at least 10 people and injured 23 others, many of them women and children. According to the Houthi-run health ministry in north-western Yemen, a total of 141 people had been killed in Saudi strikes over the past seven weeks. The government's health ministry, meanwhile, said last week that at least 1,282 people had been killed in the conflict across Yemen since 6 August. In Saudi Arabia, at least 19 people have been killed in Houthi attacks targeting the kingdom's airports since the beginning of October. Yemen has been devastated by a civil war that began in 2014, when the Houthis ousted the government from the capital, Sanaa. The conflict escalated in 2015, after the Saudi-led coalition intervened in an attempt to restore the government's rule. A four-year-old informal ceasefire began to unravel in July, when the Houthis announced a "maritime embargo" against Saudi Arabia and began missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers in the Red Sea. The Houthis said they were retaliating for what they call a Saudi blockade of their territory, as well as an air strike on Sanaa airport that they blamed on the kingdom. Related topics
